evidence.source: after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me
evidence.target: they appointed that Paul and Barnabas should go up, & certain others of the rest, to the Apostles and Priests unto Jerusalem, upon this question

2:1.note: Paul's own account of going up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas is the council journey Luke tells in Acts 15. The two accounts differ in emphasis — Paul's revelation and Titus, Luke's question from Antioch — and are entered as parallel, not harmonized.

evidence.source: after three years I came to Jerusalem to see Peter: and tarried with him fifteen days
evidence.target: Barnabas took him & brought him to the Apostles, and told them how in the way he had seen our Lord

1:18.note: Paul's first Jerusalem visit, to see Peter, is the visit Luke tells from the other side: Barnabas bringing the feared convert to the apostles and telling the Damascus story for him.

evidence.source: peace upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
evidence.target: peace upon Israel.

6:16.note: Paul's benediction on the Israel of God closes with the processional psalm's own last words: peace upon Israel.

evidence.source: But that Jerusalem which is above, is free; which is our mother.
evidence.target: And I John saw the holy city Jerusalem new descending from heaven, prepared of God, as a bride adorned for her husband.

4:26.note: The Jerusalem above, free and mother of the faithful, is the city John at last sees descending: above become come-down, in the bride's adornment.

evidence.source: in thee shall all nations be blessed
evidence.target: Shall be Blessed All The Nations of The Earth

evidence.source: Bear ye one another's burdens: and so you shall fulfill the law of Christ.
evidence.target: we that are the stronger, must sustain the infirmities of the weak

6:2.note: Bearing one another's burdens in Galatians is the same law of Christ as the strong sustaining the weak in Romans.

evidence.source: they that are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.
evidence.target: Abram believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice.

3:7.note: Those of faith are Abraham's children because Abraham himself was justified by the believing recorded in Genesis 15.

evidence.source: then are you the seed of Abraham, heirs according to promise.
evidence.target: IN Thy Seed Shall be Blessed All The Nations of The Earth

3:29.note: Heirs according to promise in Galatians inherit the blessing sworn to Abraham's seed after the offering of Isaac.

evidence.source: There is not Jew nor Greek, there is not bond nor free, there is not male nor female. For all you are one in Christ Jesus.
evidence.target: there is not, Gentile & Jew, circumcision and prepuce, Barbarous and Scythian, bond and free: but all, and in all Christ.

3:28.note: Both letters list the old divisions abolished in Christ, in nearly the same catalogue and with the same conclusion.

evidence.source: I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me.
evidence.target: our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin may be destroyed

2:20.note: Christ living in the believer in Galatians rests on the old man crucified with him in Romans.

evidence.source: all that take the sword shall perish with the sword
evidence.target: Whosoever shall shed man's blood, his blood shall be shed: for to the image of God man was made

26:52.note: The Lord's word in Gethsemane restates the flood covenant's law: blood for blood, and its reason — man made to the image of God.

evidence.source: Judas begat Phares and Zaram of Thamar
evidence.target: the other came forth: and the woman said: Why is the partition divided for thee? And for this cause called his name Phares

1:3.note: Matthew's genealogy keeps Thamar and her twins in the royal line: Phares, named for the partition divided at his birth.

evidence.source: they are dead that sought the life of the child
evidence.target: they are all dead that sought thy life

2:20.note: The angel's word to Joseph repeats, nearly word for word, God's word to Moses in Madian; Matthew draws the parallel between the two children himself.

evidence.source: He that shall curse father or mother, dying let him die
evidence.target: He that curseth his father, or mother, dying let him die

15:4.note: The Lord quotes the law of the cursing child in its own words, beside the fifth commandment (which the seed already carries at 20:12).

evidence.source: there came they that received the didrachmes
evidence.target: half a sicle according to the measure of the temple. A sicle hath twenty oboles. The half part of a sicle shall be offered to the Lord

17:23.note: The didrachma the collectors seek from the Lord is the half-shekel first imposed at the numbering in Exodus — every man's ransom 'offered to the Lord'; the Lord's answer turns on who truly owes it. (In this corpus the collectors' question stands at Matthew 17:23.)

evidence.source: You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.
evidence.target: eye for eye, tooth for tooth he shall restore

5:38.note: The Lord quotes the talion clause of Leviticus 24 — the law of retaliation that follows the blasphemer's case — before his own 'But I say to you not to resist evil'.

evidence.source: Again you have heard that it was said to them of old, Thou shalt not commit perjury: but thou shall perform thy oaths to our Lord.
evidence.target: Thou shalt not forswear thyself in my name, nor pollute the name of thy God

5:34.note: The old saying the Lord cites is Leviticus' ban on swearing falsely by God's name; its second half also gathers the law of vows performed (Numbers 30). In this corpus the oath saying stands at Matthew 5:34; the seed keys that verse to the neighbouring 19:11, but the perjury clause itself is 19:12.

evidence.source: but thou shall perform thy oaths to our Lord
evidence.target: all that he promised he shall fulfill

5:34.note: The second half of the old saying in the Sermon — perform thy oaths to the Lord — is the vow law of this verse. Its perjury half is already keyed to Leviticus 19:12 in our layer; in this corpus the saying stands at Matthew 5:34.

evidence.source: I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us if thou be Christ the Son of God
evidence.target: If a soul sin, and hear the voice of one swearing, and be witness, because either he himself saw, or is privy to it: unless he utter it, he shall bear his iniquity

26:63.note: Caiaphas puts Jesus under adjuration — the solemn 'voice of one swearing' of Leviticus 5:1, which binds the hearer who is privy to the matter to utter it or bear his iniquity. Jesus, who had held his peace, answers under it.

evidence.source: I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us if thou be Christ the Son of God.
evidence.target: Art thou Christ the Son of the blessed God?

26:63.note: Jesus before the high priest (Matthew 26:57-68; Mark 14:53-65): Jesus stands questioned before the high priest; the high priest adjures him to say if he be Christ the Son of God.

evidence.source: I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us if thou be Christ the Son of God.
evidence.target: Art thou then the Son of God? Who said: You say that I am.

26:63.note: Jesus before the high priest (Matthew 26:57-68; Luke 22:66-71): Jesus stands questioned before the high priest; Luke's side is the formal hearing at morning, where the council asks if he is the Son of God and he answers, You say that I am.

evidence.source: I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us if thou be Christ the Son of God.
evidence.target: The high Priest therefore asked Jesus of his Disciples, and of his doctrine.

26:63.note: Jesus before the high priest (Matthew 26:57-68; John 18:19-24): Jesus stands questioned before the high priest; John's side is the questioning before Annas, who asks Jesus of his disciples and of his doctrine.

evidence.source: Then the high Priest rent his garments, saying: He hath blasphemed
evidence.target: he shall not rent his garments

26:65.note: At the verdict the high priest does the one thing Leviticus forbids the anointed high priest to do, even in mourning: he rents his garments.

evidence.source: For we have seen his star in the East, and are come to adore him.
evidence.target: A star Shall Rise out of Jacob, and a rod shall arise from Israel

2:2.note: The star the Sages follow to Bethlehem is Balaam's star, risen out of Jacob in the last of his parables. Our Genesis stage already keys Jacob's own blessing (Gen 49:10) to this verse; the sighting itself was still unkeyed.

evidence.source: And seeing the multitudes, he pitied them; because they were vexed, and lay like sheep that have not a shepherd
evidence.target: lest the people of our Lord be as sheep without a pastor

9:36.note: The compassion of Jesus over the multitudes speaks Moses' prayer back to him — sheep without a shepherd — and answers it in his own person, the man provided to go in and out before them.

evidence.source: they were vexed, and lay like sheep that have not a shepherd
evidence.target: my sheep were dispersed, because there was no Pastor

9:36.note: Sheep with no shepherd, dispersed for want of a pastor: Matthew's compassion sentence is Ezechiel's diagnosis. Our layer carries this verse of Ezechiel to Numbers 27:17 (Moses' prayer) from the other side; the evangelist's use was unkeyed.

evidence.source: For the poor you have always with you: but me you have not always.
evidence.target: There shall not want poor in the land of thy habitation: therefore I command thee that thou open thy hand to thy needy and poor brother

26:11.note: The Lord's 'the poor you have always with you' is Deuteronomy's standing fact — the poor shall not cease out of the land — spoken over the ointment at Bethany. Mark's telling of the same saying is set aside; this entry carries it.

evidence.source: and his Disciples being hungry, began to pluck the ears, and to eat.
evidence.target: If thou enter into thy friend's corn, thou shalt break the ears, and rub them in thy hand: but with a sickle thou shalt not reap.

12:1.note: What the disciples do in the cornfield is exactly what this law permits: ears broken by hand and eaten on the spot, no sickle. The day's controversy is the sabbath, not the plucking — the plucking was always lawful.

evidence.source: his Disciples being hungry, began to pluck the ears, and to eat
evidence.target: The Sabboth was made for man, and not man for the Sabboth

12:1.note: Plucking ears of corn on the Sabbath — parallel accounts at Matthew 12:1-8 and Mark 2:23-28: in each, the disciples pluck ears of corn on the Sabbath and Jesus defends them, declaring the Son of man Lord of the Sabbath.

evidence.source: his Disciples being hungry, began to pluck the ears, and to eat
evidence.target: the Son of man is Lord of the Sabboth also

12:1.note: Plucking ears of corn on the Sabbath — parallel accounts at Matthew 12:1-8 and Luke 6:1-5: in each, the disciples pluck ears of corn on the Sabbath and Jesus defends them, declaring the Son of man Lord of the Sabbath.

evidence.source: And Salmon begat Booz of Rahab.
evidence.target: But Rahab the harlot and the house of her father, and all that she had, Josue caused to live, and they dwelt in the midst of Israel until this present day

1:5.note: The genealogy names Rahab as Booz's mother; Josue's book is where she is spared and dwells in Israel to this day, which is how she stands in the line at all. Her faith is keyed by the seed at Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25 to chapter 2; her preservation into the genealogy is this verse.

evidence.source: And Booz begat Obed of Ruth. And Obed begat Jesse.
evidence.target: called his name Obed: this is the father of Isai, the father of David.

1:5.note: Matthew's line runs Booz begat Obed of Ruth, and Obed begat Jesse; Ruth's book closes on that same birth, the neighbours naming Obed, father of Isai (Jesse), father of David. The seed carries Matthew 1:3 to Ruth 4:18's genealogy list; the birth verse itself was unkeyed.

evidence.source: And David the king begat Salomon of her that was the wife of Urias.
evidence.target: David sent and brought her in into his house, & she became his wife, and she bare him a son:

1:6.note: Matthew refuses Bethsabee's name and calls her her that was the wife of Urias — the genealogy itself points at the adultery. The verse it points to is this one: David bringing Urias's wife into his house after the mourning. Solomon's later birth to her is keyed by the seed at 2 Kings 12:24; the Urias clause belongs here.

evidence.source: there appeared to them Moyses and Elias talking with him.
evidence.target: Elias ascended by a hurl wind into heaven.

17:3.note: Elias appears on the mountain because his earthly exit was not death but being taken up; the parallel rests on that, and shares no wording beyond his name.

evidence.source: unto the blood of Zacharias the son of Barachias, whom you murdered between the temple & the altar.
evidence.target: they threw stones according to the king's commandment, in the court of the house of our Lord.

23:35.note: The Zacharias stoned in the temple court is Joiada's son in Chronicles. Stated openly: Matthew names him son of Barachias, Chronicles son of Joiada — the texts are not harmonised here. The seed keys both Matthew 23:35 and Luke 11:51 to the dying words at 24:22; the stoning itself stands at 24:21.

evidence.source: she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Salomon
evidence.target: And all the earth desired to see Salomon's face, that they might hear his wisdom, which God had given in his heart.

12:42.note: The seed keys the queen's coming itself (Matthew 12:42 and Luke 11:31 to 3 Kings 10:1); this anchors the hearing of the wisdom, which is the Lord's own point, in the chapter's summary verse. Luke's telling is set aside as this entry's duplicate.

evidence.source: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
evidence.target: God my God have respect to me: why hast thou forsaken me?

27:46.note: The cry from the cross. This corpus counts the psalm's title as verse 1, so the cry stands at 21:2; the seed keys Mark 15:34 to the title verse 21:1.

evidence.source: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of our Lord.
evidence.target: Blessed be he that cometh in the name of our Lord.

23:39.note: Jesus takes the festal greeting on his own lips as the condition of Jerusalem seeing him again; on the corpus numbering see the Luke 19:38 entry.

evidence.source: they gave him wine to drink mingled with gall.
evidence.target: And they gave gall for my meat:

27:34.note: Matthew's gall answers the psalm's gall; the vinegar half of the same psalm verse is keyed from John 19:28 in the seed.

evidence.source: he came unto them walking upon the sea.
evidence.target: He that alone spreadeth the heaven, & goeth upon the waves of the sea.

14:25.note: What Job confesses of God alone — going upon the waves of the sea — the Lord does on the lake in the fourth watch. Mark's and John's tellings of the same walking are set aside; Matthew's carries the verse.

evidence.source: whosoever shall see a woman to lust after her, hath already committed adultery with her in his heart.
evidence.target: I have made a covenant with mine eyes, that I would not so much as think of a virgin.

5:29.note: Job's defence begins with the covenant he made with his eyes not so much as to think of a virgin; the Lord's sermon names the same look adultery already committed in the heart. Corpus numbering: the looking saying stands at Matthew 5:29 in this text, one verse later than in modern editions.

evidence.source: as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.
evidence.target: He lendeth our Lord that hath mercy on the poor: and he will repay him the like.

25:40.note: Graded theme, honestly: the link is the identification, not shared wording. The proverb says mercy to the poor is a loan to the Lord, repaid by him; the King in the judgment names the mechanism — done to the least brethren, it was done to me.

evidence.source: Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the Kingdom of their Father.
evidence.target: the path of the just, as shining light, proceedeth even to perfect day.

13:43.note: The proverb's path of the just, shining light proceeding to perfect day, reaches its day in the Lord's word: then shall the just shine as the sun in the Father's kingdom.

evidence.source: Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the Kingdom of their Father
evidence.target: they that be learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars unto perpetual eternities

13:43.note: The just shining at the harvest's end: Daniel's learned who instruct many to justice shine as the firmament's brightness and as stars; Jesus gathers the shining into one sun-like blaze in the Father's kingdom.

evidence.source: And when you are praying, speak not much, as the Heathen. For they think that in their much-speaking they may be heard.
evidence.target: For God is in heaven, and thou upon the earth: therefore let thy words be few.

6:7.note: The Lord's prayer-teaching — speak not much, for the heathen think they are heard for much-speaking — is the Preacher's ground stated from heaven's side: God is in heaven, thou upon earth, therefore let thy words be few.

evidence.source: planted a vineyard, and made a hedge round about it, and digged in it a press, and builded a tower, and let it out to husbandmen
evidence.target: The peace-maker had a vineyard, in that which hath peoples: he delivered the same to keepers

21:33.note: Graded parallel, with the parable's other source named: the hedge, press and tower are Isaias 5's; what the Canticle shares with the parable is the vineyard delivered to keepers — the peace-maker's (Solomon's) vineyard let out, as the householder lets his out to husbandmen.

evidence.source: Consider the lilies of the field how they grow
evidence.target: I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys.

6:28.note: The Lord bids his disciples consider the lilies of the field; the bride names herself with the field's own flower — the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys. Graded allusion on the field-and-lily pairing, stated as such.

evidence.source: the people that sat in darkness, hath seen great light
evidence.target: The people that walked in darkness, hath seen great light

4:16.note: Matthew completes his Galilee citation (the seed keys 4:15 to 9:1): the people in darkness see the great light, in both tellings risen on those in the shadow of death.

evidence.source: With hearing shall you hear; and you shall not understand
evidence.target: Hear ye that hear, and understand not

13:14.note: Matthew names the prophecy fulfilled in the parables' hearers. The seed carries Mark's, Luke's and Acts' forms of the hardening word; Matthew's own full citation was unkeyed.

evidence.source: the heart of this people is waxed gross, and with their ears they have heavily heard, and their eyes they have shut
evidence.target: Blind the heart of this people, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes

13:15.note: The second half of Matthew's citation: gross heart, heavy ears, shut eyes, lest they see, hear, understand and be healed.

evidence.source: He shall not contend, nor cry out, neither shall any man hear in the streets his voice
evidence.target: He shall not cry, nor accept person, neither shall his voice be heard abroad

12:19.note: Matthew's long Servant citation, verse by verse: the seed keys only its opening (12:18 to 42:1). The quiet voice, heard by no man abroad, is 42:2's.

evidence.source: The reed bruised he shall not break, & smoking flax he shall not extinguish
evidence.target: The bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench

12:20.note: The bruised reed and smoking flax, carried over almost word for word.

evidence.source: And in his name the Gentiles shall hope
evidence.target: and the islands shall expect his law

12:21.note: The citation's close. Matthew, following the Greek, reads hope in his name where this corpus's Isaias reads the islands expecting his law — the divergence is stated, not smoothed; the verse and the expectation are the same.

evidence.source: And he answered him not to any word
evidence.target: he shall be dumb, & shall not open his mouth

27:14.note: Before Pilate the silence itself fulfils the portrait: as a lamb before his shearer, dumb, opening not his mouth. Mark 15:5's parallel silence is set aside as this entry's synoptic duplicate.

evidence.source: Then did they spit on his face, and buffeted him
evidence.target: my cheeks to the pluckers: I have not turned away my face from the rebukers & spitters

26:67.note: Spit upon, buffeted, smitten on the face before the council: the Servant gave his cheeks to the pluckers and did not turn his face from the spitters.

evidence.source: I was an hungered, and you gave me to eat
evidence.target: Break thy bread to the hungry

25:35.note: The King's reckoning — I was hungry and you gave me to eat — is Isaias's true fast read back as judgement: break thy bread to the hungry. The seed points Matthew 25 at this verse at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here.

evidence.source: the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light
evidence.target: the sun is darkened in his rising, and the moon shall not shine in her light

24:29.note: The tribulation discourse's darkened sun and lightless moon are Babylon's oracle astronomy. The seed keys this verse of Matthew to Ezechiel 32:7; Isaias 13:10 is the saying's first home, and Ezechiel's reuse of it is entered in this draft.

evidence.source: the stars shall fall from Heaven
evidence.target: all their host shall fall away as the leaf falleth from the vine

24:29.note: The falling stars of the same sentence are Edom's oracle: the host of heaven falling away as leaves from vine and fig tree.

evidence.source: Heaven and earth shall pass, but my words shall not pass
evidence.target: the heavens shall melt as smoke, and the earth shall be worn away as a garment

24:35.note: Heaven and earth passing, while what God speaks stands for ever: Isaias's heavens melting as smoke and earth wearing away, his salvation and justice never failing.

evidence.source: you shall find rest to your souls
evidence.target: you shall find refreshing for your souls

11:29.note: Find rest for your souls: Jesus' yoke saying closes with Jeremias's old-paths promise, refreshing for your souls to those who walk the good way. The seed points Matthew 11 at this verse at chapter level; the verse anchor is entered here. Ecclesiasticus 51:34's yoke, in our layer, points to the same verse of Matthew from the other side.

evidence.source: he shall separate them one from another, as the pastor separateth the sheep from the goats
evidence.target: Behold I judge between beast & beast, of rams, & of buck goats

25:32.note: The Son of man separating sheep from goats enacts Ezechiel's judgement between beast and beast, rams and buck-goats, within the shepherd oracle whose scattered-flock half the seed and our layer already key.

evidence.source: goeth to seek that which is strayed
evidence.target: That which was lost, I will seek: & that which was cast away, I will bring again

18:12.note: The shepherd leaving the ninety-nine to seek the strayed sheep walks Ezechiel's promise. Luke 15:4's form of the parable is set aside as this entry's synoptic duplicate.

evidence.source: the graves were opened: and many bodies of the saints that had slept, rose
evidence.target: Behold I will open your graves, and will bring you out of your sepulchres o my people

27:52.note: At the crucifixion the graves opening and saints rising enact, ahead of the general resurrection, Ezechiel's promise over the dry bones: I will open your graves and bring you out of your sepulchres.

evidence.source: many bodies of the saints that had slept, rose
evidence.target: many of those, that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake

evidence.source: they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of Heaven with much power and majesty
evidence.target: with the clouds of heaven there came in, as it were the son of man

24:30.note: The Olivet sign itself: the Son of man coming in heaven's clouds is Daniel's night vision seen from its far side. The seed keys Matthew 26:64 and Mark 13:26 to this verse; the discourse's own occurrence was unkeyed.

evidence.source: they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of Heaven with much power and majesty
evidence.target: they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds, with much power and glory

24:30.note: The coming of the Son of Man in glory (Matthew 24:29-31; Mark 13:24-27): both foretell the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power.

evidence.source: they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of Heaven with much power and majesty
evidence.target: they shall see the Son of man coming in a cloud with great power and majesty

24:30.note: The coming of the Son of Man in glory (Matthew 24:29-31; Luke 21:25-28): both foretell the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power.

evidence.source: when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the Angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his majesty
evidence.target: thrones were set, and the ancient of days sat

25:31.note: Thrones set for judgement in Daniel; the Son of man come in majesty and sitting on his majesty's seat in Matthew: the judgement session is one scene in two tellings.

evidence.source: the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the holy place
evidence.target: the abomination to desolation shall be set up

24:15.note: Jesus names Daniel the prophet for the abomination of desolation; Daniel speaks it three times. The seed keys this verse of Matthew to 9:27; the set-up of the abomination after the continual sacrifice is taken away is 12:11's form, and 11:31's is entered next.

evidence.source: the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the holy place
evidence.target: shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the continual sacrifice: and they shall give abomination into desolation

24:15.note: The sanctuary polluted, the continual sacrifice taken away, the abomination given into desolation: 11:31 is the form of Daniel's saying that the Machabean fulfilment (in our layer at 1 Machabees 1:57) enacted.

evidence.source: these shall go into punishment everlasting: but the just, into life everlasting
evidence.target: some unto life everlasting, & others unto reproach to see it always

25:46.note: Life everlasting against everlasting reproach: Matthew's closing sentence of the judgement is Daniel's two awakenings in the Lord's own words.

evidence.source: great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the world until now, neither shall be
evidence.target: a time shall come such as hath not been from the time since nations began even until that time

24:21.note: A tribulation such as hath not been: Daniel's time of trouble, unexampled since nations began, taken up by the Lord as the measure of the last distress.

evidence.source: they gave them into the potter's field, as our Lord did appoint to me
evidence.target: cast it forth to the statuary, a goodly price, that I was priced at by them

27:10.note: Matthew's fulfilment note: the seed carries Matthew 27:9 -> Zacharias 11:12 (the thirty pieces weighed); the disposal of the price — to the statuary/potter, in the Lord's house — is 11:13's, entered here. 'Statuary' is this corpus's word where Matthew says the potter's field.

evidence.source: he shall save his people from their sins
evidence.target: he shall redeem Israel, from all his iniquities

1:21.note: The angel explains the name Jesus out of the De profundis promise: he shall save his people from their sins, as the psalm's God 'shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.'

evidence.source: she shall bring forth a Son: and thou shalt call his name Jesus
evidence.target: she brought forth her first begotten son, and swaddled him in cloths, and laid him down in a manger

1:21.note: The birth of Jesus — Matthew's account (1:18-25) and Luke's account (2:1-20): Matthew gives the angel's word to Joseph that Mary shall bring forth a son to be named Jesus, while Luke narrates the birth itself, the child swaddled and laid in a manger.

evidence.source: as Jonas was in the whale's belly three days and three nights; so shall the Son of man be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights
evidence.target: Jonas was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights

12:40.note: The sign of Jonas rests on this verse's three days and three nights in the fish's belly. The seed keys Matthew 12:40 to Jonas 2:2 (the prayer that follows); the belly verse in this corpus is 2:1.

evidence.source: Out of Ægypt have I called my Son
evidence.target: out of Ægypt I called my son

2:15.note: Matthew quotes Osee's Exodus word — 'out of Egypt I called my son' — of the child brought back from Egypt. In its own place the son is Israel; Matthew reads the nation's pattern in the true Son.

evidence.source: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is made into the head of the corner
evidence.target: The stone, which the builders rejected: the same is made into the head of the corner

21:42.note: The Lord quotes the rejected stone in the psalm's own words. The seed keys this verse of Matthew to Psalms 117:21 (the confession verse) — apparently the margin's verse misread; the stone stands at 117:22 in this corpus, and Mark's and Luke's forms are the seed's at that verse.

evidence.source: they that passed by, blasphemed him, wagging their heads
evidence.target: they have spoken with the lips, & wagged the head

27:39.note: The passers-by at the cross wag their heads as the psalm's scorners do — 'all that see me have scorned me... and wagged the head'. The seed carries the neighbouring taunt (27:43 to 21:9); the wagging itself was unkeyed.

evidence.source: for it is written: That he will give his Angels charge of thee
evidence.target: Because he hath given his Angels charge of thee: that they keep thee in all thy ways

4:6.note: Satan himself quotes the psalm's angel-charge in the second temptation. The seed carries Luke's telling of the same quotation (4:10); Matthew's was unkeyed.

evidence.source: a man's enemies, they of his own household
evidence.target: a man's enemies they of his own household

10:36.note: The Lord takes Micheas' sentence whole: a man's enemies, they of his own household. Luke's telling expands the list (next entry); Matthew keeps the prophet's closing words verbatim.

evidence.source: then will he render to every man according to his works
evidence.target: thou wilt render to every one according to his works

16:27.note: The Son of man's rendering to every man according to his works is the psalm's confession about God himself: 'thou wilt render to every one according to his works.' Paul's use at Romans 2:6 stands on the same clause.

evidence.source: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven

evidence.source: Lo the sinners themselves, and they that abound in the world, have obtained riches.
evidence.target: Why then do the impious live, are they advanced, & strengthened with riches?

72:12.note: Asaph's psalm is built on Job's question: sinners abounding in the world and obtaining riches is the spectacle that nearly made his feet slip (72:2-3).

evidence.source: Who giveth to beasts their food: and to the young ravens that call upon him.
evidence.target: Who prepareth for the raven her meat, when her young ones cry to God

146:9.note: The psalm answers the whirlwind's question with praise: the God who asked who prepares the raven's meat is confessed as the one who feeds the young ravens that call upon him.

evidence.source: Thou hast set a bound, which they shall not pass over
evidence.target: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt not proceed farther, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves.

103:9.note: The creation psalm confesses as praise what the whirlwind declares as command: a bound set for the sea — hitherto shalt thou come, and no farther.

evidence.source: Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, o Lord, and shalt teach out of thy law.
evidence.target: Blessed is the man that is corrected of God: refuse not therefore the chastising of our Lord

93:12.note: Eliphaz's beatitude — blessed the man corrected of God — becomes the psalm's blessed man instructed and taught out of the law. James 1:10 is keyed to this verse of Job by the seed's margin on other grounds; the psalm's taking of the beatitude was unkeyed.

evidence.source: Words of our Lord be chaste words: silver examined by fire, tried from the earth, purged seven fold.
evidence.target: Every word of God tried by fire, is a buckler to them that hope in him

11:7.note: Agur's confession — every word of God tried by fire — is the psalm's silver examined by fire and purged sevenfold, carried from the psalmist's trouble into the proverb. The seed carries the psalm only at chapter level (Proverbs 30).

evidence.source: The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment.
evidence.target: She hath opened her mouth to wisdom, and the law of clemency is in her tongue.

36:30.note: The valiant woman's portrait closes the Proverbs with the psalm's just man in feminine form: a mouth opened to wisdom, a tongue carrying the law of clemency where the psalm's tongue speaks judgment. The seed carries the psalm only at chapter level (Proverbs 31).

evidence.source: he was compared to beasts without understanding, and became like to them.
evidence.target: there is one death of man, and beasts, and the condition of both equal: as man dieth, so they also die

48:13.note: The wisdom psalm's refrain — man in honour compared to beasts and become like them — is the Preacher's sentence in brief: one death of man and beasts, and the condition of both equal.

evidence.source: why hast thou forsaken me?
evidence.target: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

evidence.source: they have divided my garments among them: and upon my vesture they have cast lot.
evidence.target: They have parted my garments among them: and upon my vesture they have cast lots.

evidence.target: I will declare thy name to my brethren: in the midst of the Church will I praise thee.

evidence.source: they have spoken with the lips, & wagged the head.
evidence.target: blasphemed him, wagging their heads,

evidence.source: He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: let him save him
evidence.target: He trusted in God; let him now deliver him if he will

evidence.source: let him deliver him: let him save him, because he will him.
evidence.target: he will defend him, & will deliver him from the hands of the adversaries.

evidence.source: Thy seat o God for ever and ever: a rod of direction the rod of thy Kingdom.
evidence.target: Thy throne o God for ever and ever: a rod of equity, the rod of thy kingdom.

evidence.target: Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: therefore thee, God, thy God hath anointed with the oil of exultation above thy fellows.

evidence.target: into all the earth hath the sound of them gone forth: and unto the ends of the whole world the words of them.

evidence.source: that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.
evidence.target: That thou mayest be justified in thy words, and overcome when thou art judged.

evidence.source: there is no fear of God before his eyes.
evidence.target: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

evidence.source: All have declined, they are become unprofitable together: there is not that doth good, no there is not one.
evidence.target: All have declined, they are become unprofitable together: there is not that doeth good, there is not so much as one.

evidence.source: In the beginning, o Lord, thou didst found the earth: and the heavens are the works of thy hands.
evidence.target: Thou in the beginning o Lord didst found the earth: and the works of thy hands are the heavens.

evidence.source: but thou art the self-same, and thy years shall not fail.
evidence.target: but thou art the self-same, and thy years shall not fail.

evidence.source: Which makest spirits thine Angels: and thy ministers a burning fire.
evidence.target: He that maketh his Angels, spirits: and his ministers, a flame of fire.

evidence.source: Adore him all ye his Angels:
evidence.target: let all the Angels of God adore him.

evidence.source: I said: You are gods
evidence.target: I said, you are gods?

evidence.source: I will open my mouth in parables:
evidence.target: I will open my mouth in parables,

evidence.source: Our Lord is my helper: I will not fear what man can do to me.
evidence.target: Our Lord is my helper: I will not fear what man shall do to me.

evidence.source: I believed, for which cause I spake:
evidence.target: I believed, for the which cause I have spoken,

evidence.source: The stone, which the builders rejected: the same is made into the head of the corner.
evidence.target: The stone which the builders rejected, the same is made into the head of the corner?

evidence.target: This is the stone that was rejected of you the builders: which is made into the head of the corner:

evidence.source: This was done by our Lord: and it is marvelous in our eyes.
evidence.target: By our Lord was this done, and it is marvelous in our eyes.

evidence.source: then said I, Behold I come. In the head of the book it is written of me,
evidence.target: Then said I, Behold I come: in the head of the book it is written of me:

evidence.source: The earth is our Lord's, and the fullness thereof:
evidence.target: The earth is our Lord's, and the fullness thereof.

evidence.source: Stay thy tongue from evil: and thy lips that they speak not guile.
evidence.target: let him refrain his tongue from evil, & his lips that they speak not guile.

evidence.source: Turn away from evil, and do good: seek after peace and pursue it.
evidence.target: Let him decline from evil, and do good: let him inquire peace, & follow it:

evidence.source: The eyes of our Lord upon the just: and his ears unto their prayers.
evidence.target: the eyes of our Lord are upon the just, and his ears unto their prayers:

evidence.source: the countenance of our Lord is upon them that do evil things:
evidence.target: the countenance of our Lord upon them that do evil things.

evidence.source: Taste ye, and see that our Lord is sweet:
evidence.target: you have tasted that our Lord is sweet.

evidence.source: he hath given his Angels charge of thee: that they keep thee in all thy ways.
evidence.target: he will give his Angels charge of thee,

evidence.target: in their hands shall they hold thee up, lest perhaps thou knock thy foot against a stone.

evidence.target: thou art a Priest for ever

evidence.source: Today if ye shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
evidence.target: Today if you shall hear his voice, do not obdurate your hearts

evidence.source: a thousand years before thine eyes, are as yesterday that is past.
evidence.target: one day with our Lord is as a thousand years, & a thousand years as one day.

evidence.source: All nations whatsoever thou hast made, shall come, and shall adore before thee, o Lord:
evidence.target: all nations shall come, and adore in thy sight,

evidence.source: Our Lord hath made known his salvation: in the sight of the Gentiles he hath revealed his justice.
evidence.target: all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.

evidence.source: All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
evidence.target: mine eyes have seen thy Salvation,

evidence.source: From the rising of the sun unto the going down, the name of our Lord is laudable.
evidence.target: from the rising of the sun even to the going down, great is my name among the Gentiles,

evidence.source: until I find a place for our Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
evidence.target: he might find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

evidence.source: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.
evidence.target: thou that didst make Heaven & earth, the sea, and all things that are in them,

evidence.source: In thee o Lord I have hoped, let me not be confounded for ever:
evidence.target: In thee o Lord have I hoped, let me not be confounded for ever:

evidence.source: Be unto me for a God protector, and for a fenced place: that thou mayst save me:
evidence.target: Be unto me for a God protector: and for a house of refuge, that thou mayst save me.

evidence.target: God hath spoken in his holy: I shall rejoice, and shall divide Sichem: and shall measure the valley of tabernacles.

evidence.target: Give us aid from tribulation: because man's salvation is vain.

evidence.source: In God we shall do strength: and he will bring our enemies to nothing.
evidence.target: In God we shall do strength: and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.

evidence.target: that say to me: Well, well.

evidence.target: They are corrupt, and are become abominable in their studies: there is not that doth good no not one.

evidence.source: Praising I will invocate our Lord: & I shall be saved from mine enemies.
evidence.target: Our Lord praise-worthy will I invocate: and from mine enemies I shall be saved.

evidence.source: For who is God but our Lord? Or who is God but our God?
evidence.target: Who is God beside our Lord: and who is strong beside our God?

evidence.target: Bring to our Lord ye families of peoples: bring to our Lord glory and empire.

evidence.target: let them say among nations, Our Lord hath reigned.

evidence.target: Confess ye to our Lord, and invocate his name: make his inventions known among the peoples.

evidence.target: Confess ye to our Lord, because he is good: because his mercy is for ever.

evidence.target: why art thou sorrowful, o my soul? And why dost thou trouble me? Hope in God, because yet will I confess to him: the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

evidence.source: for ever will I prepare thy seed. And I will build thy seat unto generation and generation.
evidence.target: He shall build a house to my name, and I will establish the throne of his Kingdom for ever.

evidence.source: He shall invocate me: Thou art my Father: my God,

evidence.source: The revenge of the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed:

evidence.source: Praise ye him sun and moon: praise him all ye stars, and light.
evidence.target: Sun and moon bless ye our Lord: praise and superexalt him for ever.

evidence.source: Create a clean heart in me, o God: and renew a right spirit in my bowels.
evidence.target: I will give you a new heart, and will put a new spirit in the midst of you:

evidence.target: the smoke of the incenses of the prayers of the saints ascended

140:2.note: The psalm's prayer offered as incense before God's sight is realised in the Apocalypse, where the smoke of the incense rises with the saints' prayers before God.

evidence.source: he said, and they were made: he commanded and they were created,
evidence.target: And God said: Be light made. And light was made.

evidence.source: Lord what is man, that thou art made known to him?
evidence.target: What is man that thou magnifiest him?

evidence.source: All have declined, they are become unprofitable together: there is not that doth good
evidence.target: All have declined, they are become unprofitable together: there is not that doth good

13:3.note: Psalms 13 and 52 are the same psalm in two forms, and this verse of universal corruption is word for word in both.

evidence.source: Who will give from Sion the salvation of Israel?
evidence.target: Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel?

13:7.note: The closing cry for salvation from Sion, with Jacob rejoicing and Israel glad, ends both forms of the psalm.

evidence.source: thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens, and thy truth even to the clouds
evidence.target: thy mercy is great above the heavens: & thy truth even to the clouds

56:11.note: Psalm 107 is woven from Psalms 56 and 59, and this mercy-to-the-heavens verse of Psalm 56 reappears in it almost unchanged.

evidence.source: Be exalted above the heavens o God: and thy glory upon all the earth
evidence.target: Be exalted above the heavens o God, and thy glory over all the earth

56:12.note: The exaltation refrain that closes Psalm 56 is repeated as the refrain of the Psalm 107 cento.

evidence.source: David is come into the house of Achimelech
evidence.target: And David came into Nobe to Achimelech the Priest

51:2.note: Psalm 51's title reports David's coming to Achimelech, which is the arrival at Nobe narrated in this verse.

evidence.source: when the Zipheites were come, and said to Saul: Is not David hid with us?
evidence.target: And the Zipheites went up unto Saul in Gabaa, saying: Lo, doth not David lie hid with us

53:2.note: Psalm 53's title quotes the Zipheites' report to Saul, and this verse is that report in the narrative.

evidence.source: when the foreigners held him in Geth
evidence.target: and came to Achis the king of Geth

55:1.note: Psalm 55's title places David in the hands of the foreigners at Geth, where this verse brings him to Achis its king.

evidence.source: Joab returned, and struck Idumæa
evidence.target: Joab the general of the warfare was gone up to bury them that were slain, and had slain all male kind in Idumea

59:2.note: Psalm 59's title recalls Joab's Idumean campaign, which this verse recalls again when it explains the rise of Ader the Idumeite.

evidence.source: A Psalm of David, when Absalom his son persecuted him
evidence.target: there will be no escape for us from the face of Absalom

142:1.note: Psalm 142's title sets the psalm in Absalom's persecution, and this verse is David ordering the flight from Absalom's face.

evidence.source: My protector and the horn of my salvation
evidence.target: my shield, and the horn of my salvation

17:3.note: Psalm 17 is David's song of deliverance also preserved in 2 Kings 22, and the horn-of-salvation confession stands in both forms.

evidence.source: Every man is a liar
evidence.target: every man a liar

115:2.note: Paul takes up the psalmist's confession that every man is a liar as part of his proof that God is true though man lies.

evidence.source: I will take the chalice of salvation
evidence.target: The chalice of benediction which we do bless

115:4.note: The psalmist's chalice of salvation, taken with invocation of the Lord's name, is taken up in Paul's chalice of benediction at the Lord's table.

evidence.source: Our Lord hath done magnifically with us
evidence.target: hath done great things to me

125:3.note: Mary's Magnificat echoes the psalm's thanksgiving that the Lord has done great things for his people, now done to her.

evidence.source: I will confess against me my injustice to our Lord: and thou hast forgiven the impiety of my sin
evidence.target: If we confess our sins, he is faithful & just, for to forgive us our sins

evidence.source: they that were near me, stood far off
evidence.target: all his acquaintance stood a far off

evidence.source: They have digged my hands and my feet
evidence.target: unless I see in his hands the print of the nails

21:17.note: The psalm's pierced hands and feet stand behind Thomas's demand to see the nail print in the risen Lord's hands.

evidence.source: Our Lord ruleth me
evidence.target: shall rule them, and shall conduct them to the living fountains of waters

22:1.note: The shepherd Lord who rules the psalmist becomes the Lamb on the throne who rules the redeemed and leads them to living fountains of waters.

evidence.source: all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him
evidence.target: all nations shall come, and adore in thy sight

evidence.source: Our Lord is pitiful and merciful: patient and very merciful
evidence.target: Our Lord is pitiful, and merciful: long suffering, and very merciful

144:8.note: The great mercy confession of Exodus is sung in nearly identical words by both psalms.

evidence.source: a contrite and humbled heart, o God, thou wilt not despise
evidence.target: Our Lord is nigh to them, that are of a contrite heart

evidence.source: Our Lord is nigh to them, that are of a contrite heart: and the humble of spirit he will save
evidence.target: with a contrite & humble spirit: that he may revive the spirit of the humble, and revive the heart of the contrite

33:19.note: Isaias takes up the psalm's contrite heart and humble spirit, promising that the High and Eminent dwells with them to revive them.

evidence.source: My tears have been breads unto me day and night
evidence.target: Thou wilt feed us with the bread of tears

41:4.note: The striking image of tears eaten as bread in Psalm 41 is taken up in Psalm 79's bread of tears given by God himself.

evidence.source: so doth my soul desire after thee, o God
evidence.target: My soul hath thirsted to thee

41:2.note: Both psalms open with the soul's thirsting desire for God, as the hart for the waters and as flesh thirsting in the morning watch.

evidence.source: Our Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice
evidence.target: Let the heavens be glad, and the earth rejoice: and let them say among nations, Our Lord hath reigned

96:1.note: The canticle David set before the ark in Chronicles and Psalm 96 proclaim the same reign of the Lord with the earth rejoicing.

evidence.source: Mercy and truth have met each other: justice and peace have kissed
evidence.target: Mercy and truth shall go before thy face

84:11.note: Mercy and truth are paired attendants of God's reign in both psalms, meeting and kissing in one, going before his face in the other.

evidence.source: The sins of my youth, and my ignorances do not remember. According to thy mercy remember thou me
evidence.target: Remember not our old iniquities, let thy mercies quickly prevent us

24:7.note: Both psalms plead the same prayer, that God remember mercy and not remember old sins and iniquities.

evidence.source: as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God
evidence.target: Thy children as young plants of olive-trees, round about thy table

51:10.note: The fruitful olive tree in God's house in Psalm 51 becomes the olive plants of the blessed man's children round his table in Psalm 127.

evidence.source: Which didest take sweet meats together with me
evidence.target: who did eat my breads, hath greatly trodden me under-foot

54:15.note: Psalm 54's intimate companion who shared sweet food with the psalmist is the same familiar betrayer who ate the psalmist's bread in Psalm 40.

evidence.source: The just shall flourish as a palm tree: as the cedar of Libanus shall he be multiplied
evidence.target: I am exalted as a cedar in Libanus

91:13.note: The just man flourishing as the cedar of Libanus in the psalm is the image Wisdom takes for herself in Ecclesiasticus.

evidence.source: Myrrh, and Aloes, and Cassia from thy garments
evidence.target: as a little rod of smoke of the aromatical spices of myrrh and frankincense

44:9.note: The royal bridegroom's myrrh-perfumed garments in the psalm and the bride's procession perfumed with myrrh in the Canticle share the same wedding spices.

evidence.source: This dragon, whom thou madest to delude
evidence.target: Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon

103:26.note: Both psalms confess God's mastery over the great dragon of the sea, formed by him in one and broken by him in the other.

evidence.source: Praise our Lord from the earth: ye dragons, and all depths
evidence.target: Whales, and all things that move in the waters, bless ye our Lord

148:7.note: The three children's canticle follows Psalm 148's litany, calling the sea creatures of the depths to bless and praise the Lord.

evidence.source: Who covereth the heaven with clouds: and prepareth rain for the earth
evidence.target: Who bindeth the waters in his clouds

146:8.note: Psalm and Job confess the same divine husbandry of the waters, bound in the clouds and poured as rain on the earth.

evidence.source: Thou rulest over the power of the sea: and the moving of the waves thereof thou doest mitigate
evidence.target: In his strength suddenly the seas are gathered together

88:10.note: Both texts confess that God alone rules the power of the sea and stills its waves by his strength.

evidence.source: as the flower of the field, so shall he flourish
evidence.target: Who as a flower cometh forth and is destroyed, and flyeth as a shadow

102:15.note: Man's days as the grass and flower of the field in the psalm are Job's flower that comes forth, is destroyed, and flies as a shadow.

evidence.source: brought out of the iron furnace of Ægypt
evidence.target: the hard works of clay and brick

4:20.note: Deuteronomy's 'iron furnace of Egypt' is the brick-kiln bondage of Exodus 1 named in a single image.

evidence.source: The blessing of him, that appeared in the bush
evidence.target: appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush

33:16.note: In Moses' blessing of Joseph, God is named simply as him 'that appeared in the bush' — the theophany of Exodus 3 become one of his titles.

evidence.source: thou shalt bind them as a sign on thy hand, and they shall be and shall move between thine eyes
evidence.target: it shall be as a sign in thy hand, and as a monument before thine eyes

6:8.note: The sign upon the hand and the monument before the eyes were first appointed for the memorial of the Exodus; Deuteronomy binds the words of the Law itself with the same sign.

evidence.source: and fed thee with Manna in the wilderness, which thy fathers knew not
evidence.target: Man-hu! Which signifieth: What is this! For they knew not what it was

evidence.source: who brought forth rivers out of the hardest rock
evidence.target: thou shalt strike the rock, & water shall go out thereof

evidence.source: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God, as thou didst tempt him in the place of tentation

evidence.source: thou shalt destroy his name under heaven
evidence.target: I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven

evidence.source: Give from among you wise and skillful men, and such whose conversation is approved in your tribes, that I may appoint them your princes
evidence.target: provide out of all the people men that are wise, & do fear God, in whom there is truth, and that do hate avarice, and appoint of them tribunes, and centurions

evidence.source: hath he spread his wings, and he hath taken him, and carried him on his shoulders
evidence.target: I have carried you upon the wings of eagles

evidence.source: I the Lord thy God, that brought thee out of the Land of Ægypt out of the house of servitude
evidence.target: which brought thee forth out of the Land of Ægypt, out of the house of servitude

evidence.source: as thou didst request of our Lord thy God in Horeb, when the assembly was gathered, and saidst: I will no more hear the voice of our Lord my God, and this exceeding great fire I will see no more, lest I die

evidence.source: And do you therefore love strangers because you also were strangers in the Land of Ægypt

evidence.source: two tables of stone written with the finger of God

evidence.source: I cast the tables out of my hands, and brake them in your sight
