evidence.source: great, strong, and terrible, keeping covenant and mercy
evidence.target: strong and faithful God, keeping his covenant and mercy to them that love him

evidence.source: I confess for the sins of the children of Israel, in which they have sinned to thee: I and my father's house have sinned
evidence.target: We have sinned, we have done iniquity, we have dealt impiously, and have revolted

1:6.note: Nehemias confesses his father's house and Israel's sins in the same penitential pattern as Daniel's great confession.

evidence.source: Esdras therefore the Priest brought the law before the multitude of men and women, and all that could understand
evidence.target: the people being assembled together, as well men as women, children, & strangers, that are within thy gates: that hearing they may learn

8:2.note: Esdras brings the Law before men, women and all who could understand, the assembly Deuteronomy commanded so that hearing they may learn.

evidence.source: thou hast made heaven, and all the host thereof: the earth and all things that are in it: the seas and all things that are therein
evidence.target: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them

9:6.note: The great confession opens with the Psalm confession of the Maker of heaven, earth, sea and all things in them.

evidence.source: thou sawest the affliction of our fathers in Ægypt: and their cry thou didst hear upon the Red sea
evidence.target: I have seen the affliction of my people in Ægypt, and I have heard their cry

9:9.note: Nehemias' prayer retells Exodus in God's own words to Moyses: I have seen the affliction and heard the cry.

evidence.source: because he is benign & merciful, patient and of much mercy
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

2:13.note: Joel summons Israel to return on the strength of the proclamation: 'he is benign and merciful, patient and of much mercy'.

evidence.source: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons, and your daughters shall prophesy
evidence.target: O that all the people might prophesy, and that our Lord would give them his spirit!

2:28.note: What Moses wished over Eldad and Medad — all the people prophesying, the Lord giving them his spirit — Joel promises outright: the spirit poured on all flesh. Peter preaches Joel's form at Pentecost; the wish underneath it is this verse.

evidence.source: Cut your ploughs into swords, and your spades into spears
evidence.target: they shall turn their swords into coulters, and their spears into sithes

3:10.note: Joel summons the nations to war in the exact inverse of Isaias' (and Micheas') peace oracle — the reversal only works because the original wording is in the hearer's ear.

evidence.source: I will render you the years, which the locust, the bruke, and the blast, and the eruke hath eaten: my great strength which I have sent upon you
evidence.target: the grass of the earth was devoured, and what fruits soever on the trees, which the hail had left: there was also nothing at all left that was green

2:25.note: Joel's locust host, sent by God and devouring the land bare, is the Exodus plague returned upon Israel herself; Joel promises the eaten years rendered back. Same plague-shape, graded parallel.

evidence.source: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood
evidence.target: the sun became black as it were sack-cloth of hair: and the whole moon became as blood

evidence.source: a fountain shall issue out of the house of the Lord
evidence.target: living waters shall issue forth out of Jerusalem

3:18.note: Joel's fountain issuing from the house of the Lord to water the torrent and Zacharias's living waters issuing from Jerusalem are the prophets' twin forms of the restored city's river.

evidence.source: I know that thou art a clement, and merciful God, patient, and of much compassion, and forgiving upon the evil
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

4:2.note: Jonas quotes the proclamation back at God as a complaint — 'I know that thou art a clement and merciful God, patient and of much compassion' — the formula almost word for word, turned into a grievance that Nineveh was spared.

evidence.source: out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou hast heard my voice.
evidence.target: he hath heard my voice from his holy temple: and my cry in his sight, hath entered into his ears.

2:3.note: Jonas' prayer from the fish is woven from the psalms; here the heard-cry and the temple meet. The seed keys Jonas 2:3 to Psalms 119 and 129 at chapter level.

evidence.source: I cried out of my tribulation to our Lord, & he hath heard me
evidence.target: When I was in tribulation I cried to our Lord: and he heard me

evidence.source: all thy surges, and thy waves have passed over me.
evidence.target: All thy high things, and thy ways have passed over me.

2:4.note: Jonas' waves are the psalm's waters passing over the soul. This corpus prints the psalm's word as ways where the sense is waves; the shared clause have passed over me is what is printed in both.

evidence.source: I am cast away from the sight of thine eyes: but yet I shall see thy holy temple again.
evidence.target: I am cast away from the sight of thine eyes.

2:5.note: Jonas quotes the psalm's cast-away word and answers it with his own yet I shall see thy temple.

evidence.source: The waters have compassed me even to the soul:
evidence.target: Save me, o God: because waters are entered into my soul.

2:6.note: The waters-to-the-soul of the great passion psalm, prayed again inside the fish.

evidence.source: I in the voice of praise will immolate to thee: what things soever I have vowed I will render
evidence.target: Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise, and pay thy vows to the Highest.

2:10.note: Jonas' vow from the fish is Psalm 49's sacrifice of praise and paying of vows, performed.

evidence.source: he desired for his soul to die, and said: It is better for me to die than to live
evidence.target: he desired for his soul to die, and said: It sufficeth me Lord, take my soul

4:8.note: Jonas under the ivy repeats Elias under the juniper in the same words — 'he desired for his soul to die' stands in both verses; the prophet angry at mercy sits where the prophet weary of flight sat.

evidence.source: They that keep vanities in vain, forsake their mercy
evidence.target: Thou hast hated them that observe vanities, unprofitably

evidence.source: Who knoweth if God will convert, and forgive
evidence.target: Who knoweth if he will convert, & forgive

evidence.source: God saw their works, that they were converted from their evil way
evidence.target: they did penance at the preaching of Jonas

3:10.note: The men of Nineveh who rise in the judgement did penance at Jonas's preaching — the conversion Jonas records when God saw their works and turned from their evil way.

evidence.source: Our Lord is patient, and great of strength, and cleansing, he will not make innocent
evidence.target: no man of himself is innocent before thee

1:3.note: Nahum takes the proclamation's severe edge: the Lord is patient, but 'cleansing, he will not make innocent' — Exodus: 'no man of himself is innocent before thee'.

evidence.source: Our Lord is patient, and great of strength, and cleansing, he will not make innocent
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

1:3.note: Nahum takes up the Exodus name of God — patient — but stresses its justice side: cleansing, he will by no means make the guilty innocent.

evidence.source: God is jealous, & our Lord revenging
evidence.target: The Lord his name is Jealous, God is an emulator

1:2.note: Nahum's God 'is jealous' — Exodus gives the jealousy a name: 'The Lord, his name is Jealous'.

evidence.source: Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that Evangelizeth, and preacheth peace
evidence.target: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that evangelizeth & preacheth peace

1:15.note: Nahum takes up Isaias' beautiful-feet herald against Nineveh's fall. The seed carries Nahum 1:15 -> Isaias 52 at chapter level only; Romans 10:15 quotes Isaias' form.

evidence.source: Our Lord is good, & strengthening in the day of tribulation: & knowing them that hope in him
evidence.target: Our Lord knoweth, who be his

1:7.note: The seal on God's firm foundation, 'the Lord knoweth who are his,' stands with Nahum's Lord who is good in tribulation and knows those that hope in him.

evidence.source: the children of Israel could not behold the face of Moyses for the glory of his countenance
evidence.target: seeing the face of Moyses horned, they were afraid to come near

3:7.note: Paul: the children of Israel 'could not behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance'; Exodus: seeing Moses' face — the DR prints 'horned', for the Vulgate's word — 'they were afraid to come near'.

evidence.source: when he shall be converted to our Lord, the veil shall be taken away
evidence.target: Which going in to our Lord, and speaking with him, he took away until he went forth

3:16.note: Paul reads Moses' own act spiritually: as Moses, going in before the Lord, took away the veil (named at 34:33 and 34:35) until he came forth, so 'when he shall be converted to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away'.

evidence.source: That I will dwell, and walk in them, and will be their God; and they shall be my people
evidence.target: I will walk among you, & will be your God, & you shall be my people

6:16.note: Paul's temple catena quotes the covenant promise of Leviticus 26:11-12. The seed carries this verse of Paul at 26:11 (the tabernacle clause); the walking-and-people clause stands at 26:12.

evidence.source: I will dwell, and walk in them, and will be their God; and they shall be my people
evidence.target: my tabernacle shall be in them: & I will be their God, and they shall be my people

6:16.note: Paul's temple-of-the-living-God promise is composite: its dwelling formula stands in Leviticus 26:11–12 (entered in our layer to this same verse of Ezechiel) and its tabernacle form is Ezechiel's — my tabernacle in them, I their God, they my people. Both anchors are recorded; this entry claims the tabernacle wording.

evidence.source: Bear not the yoke with infidels.
evidence.target: Thou shalt not plough with an oxe and ass together.

6:14.note: Paul's unequal yoke is the law's plough-team: an ox and an ass under one yoke, kinds that cannot pull together. The image is Deuteronomy's; the application — fellowship with unbelief — is the apostle's.

evidence.source: he that soweth sparingly, sparingly also shall reap: and he that soweth in blessings, of blessings also shall reap.
evidence.target: Some divide their own goods, and are made richer: others take violently not their own, and are always in poverty.

9:6.note: Graded parallel: Paul's sowing economy is the proverb's scattering economy — dividing one's goods and growing richer — with no shared wording beyond the shape of the law itself.

evidence.source: we must all be manifested before the judgement seat of Christ, that every one may receive the proper things of the body, according as he hath done, either good or evil.
evidence.target: all things that are done, God will bring into judgement for every error, whether it be good or evil.

5:10.note: Paul's judgment seat is the Preacher's closing sentence with its seat named: God will bring all things done into judgement, whether good or evil — every one receiving according as he hath done, either good or evil.

evidence.source: written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God: not in tables of stone, but in the tables carnal of the heart
evidence.target: in their heart I will write it

3:3.note: Paul's living epistle, written on heart-tables, is the new covenant's inscription: my law in their bowels, in their heart I will write it. The stone-tables contrast is Exodus's half of Paul's sentence; the heart-writing is Jeremias's, and only that is claimed here. The Ezechiel 36:26 anchor of the same verse is entered separately.

evidence.source: not in tables of stone, but in the tables carnal of the heart
evidence.target: will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a fleshy heart

3:3.note: Stone against flesh: Paul's not-in-stone-but-heart tables take up Ezechiel's surgery, the stony heart taken away and a fleshy heart given. The Jeremias 31:33 anchor of the same verse (the heart-writing) is entered separately.

evidence.source: through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and so escaped his hands
evidence.target: conveyed him away by the wall, letting him down in a basket

11:33.note: Paul's basket escape from Damascus in his own telling and in Luke's: let down by the wall in a basket, in the night. The seed carries 2 Corinthians 11:32 (the governor's watch) to Acts 9:24; the escape verse itself was unkeyed.

evidence.source: and you shall be my sons & daughters, saith our Lord omnipotent.
evidence.target: I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to me for a son

6:18.note: The promise to David's son — I will be to him for a father — is widened to sons and daughters; Paul weaves Ezechiel 37 and Isaias 52 around it (both seed-carried at 6:16-17), this anchor was unkeyed.

evidence.source: He that had much, abounded not: and he that had little, wanted not.
evidence.target: neither he that gathered more, had above: nor he that provided less, found under

8:15.note: The manna measure — more gathered, none over; less, none under — is Paul's rule for the collection: equality out of abundance and want.

evidence.source: who also hath sealed us, and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
evidence.target: which is the pledge of our inheritance,

1:22.note: The Spirit as pledge (the earnest-money of the inheritance) in both letters, with the sealing beside it at Ephesians 1:13 — an untranslatable-in-brief shared term, rendered 'pledge' in this corpus in both places.

evidence.source: as the serpent seduced Eve by his subtlety
evidence.target: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat

evidence.source: if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved
evidence.target: the earthly habitation presseth down the understanding

evidence.source: he that ministereth seed to the sower, will give bread also for to eat
evidence.target: giveth seed to the sower, and bread to him that eateth:

9:10.note: Paul takes up Isaias's very words about God giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater and applies them to Corinthian giving.

evidence.source: hath made us meet ministers of the new testament: not in the letter, but in the Spirit.
evidence.target: I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel

3:6.note: Paul's ministry of the new testament in the Spirit presupposes Jeremias's promise of the new covenant.

evidence.source: by him, Amen to God, unto our glory.
evidence.target: Thus saith Amen, the faithful and true witness

1:20.note: The Amen by which God's promises are confirmed in Christ in Corinthians becomes Christ's own title, Amen, in the Apocalypse.

evidence.source: we walk by faith and not by sight
evidence.target: faith is, the substance of things to be hoped for, the argument of things not appearing.

5:7.note: Walking by faith and not by sight in Corinthians is defined in Hebrews as faith's hold on things hoped for and not seen.

evidence.source: when I am weak, then am I mighty.
evidence.target: I can all things in him that strengtheneth me.

12:10.note: Paul's paradox of strength in weakness and his confession of doing all things in the one who strengthens him state the same dependence.

evidence.source: that no man should consecrate his son or daughter by fire to Moloch
evidence.target: Of thy seed thou shalt not give to be consecrated to the idol Moloch

23:10.note: Josiah defiles Topheth to end the rite Leviticus 18:21 forbids — seed consecrated to Moloch, passed through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom.

evidence.source: We therefore boiled my son, and did eat him
evidence.target: so that you shall eat the flesh of your sons & of your daughters

6:29.note: In the Samaria siege the covenant curse stops being a threat: two mothers boil and eat a son, and the king of Israel hears the case in the famine Leviticus 26:29 foretold. Ezekiel re-pronounces the same curse (entered as allusion).

evidence.source: But the money for offence, & the money for sins, they brought not into the temple of our Lord, because it was the Priests'
evidence.target: the law of both hosts shall be one: to the Priest that offereth it, it shall pertain

12:16.note: Joas's temple repairs respect the old rule: the money for offence and for sins is not treasury income, because Leviticus assigns both hosts — and their price — to the priest who offers them.

evidence.source: And he made his son pass through fire: and he used soothsaying, and observed divinations, and made pythons, and multiplied enchanters
evidence.target: Neither let there be found in thee any that shall expiate his son, or daughter, making them to pass through the fire: or that demandeth of soothsayers, and observeth dreams and divinations

21:6.note: Manasses' reign is Deuteronomy's banned list enacted item by item — the son through the fire, soothsaying, divinations, pythons. Chronicles' retelling of the same reign (2 Paralipomenon 33:6) is set aside as this entry's duplicate.

evidence.source: The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers: but every one shall die in his own sin.
evidence.target: The fathers shall not be slain for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every one shall die for his own sin,

14:6.note: Amasias spares his father's murderers' children 'according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moyses' — and the history quotes the law nearly entire. The seed points this verse at Deuteronomy 21 by chapter; the words quoted stand at 24:16.

evidence.source: Elias took his mantle, and folded it together, and smote the waters, which were divided into two parts, and they both passed over by the dry land.
evidence.target: stood girded upon the dry ground in the midst of Jordan, and all the people passed over through the dry channel.

2:8.note: Jordan opens a second time: Elias and Eliseus cross on dry ground where Israel crossed behind the ark. The river, the dry passage, and the two parts are the link; the instruments differ, mantle for ark.

evidence.source: Elias ascended by a hurl wind into heaven.
evidence.target: he walked with God, and was seen no more: because God took him.

2:11.note: Only two men leave the earth without the text recording a death: Henoch, whom God took, and Elias, taken up by the whirlwind. Graded parallel — the shape is shared, the wording is not.

evidence.source: brake the brazen serpent, which Moyses had made: for until that time the children of Israel burnt incense to it
evidence.target: Moyses therefore made A brazen Serpent, and set it for a sign

18:4.note: Ezechias destroys the very sign Moyses made, because the sign had become an idol — the verse names its maker, and Numbers is the making.

evidence.source: Make a Phase to our Lord your God, according as it is written in the Book of this covenant.
evidence.target: that thou mayest make the Phase to our Lord thy God: because in this month our Lord thy God brought thee out of Ægypt by night.

23:21.note: Josias commands the Passover 'as written' — and what is written is Deuteronomy's command to make the Phase to the Lord thy God. Centralised at Jerusalem, as Deuteronomy requires and Samuel-era practice had not been.

evidence.source: It is the sepulchre of the man of God, which came from Juda, and foretold these things which thou hast done upon the altar of Bethel.
evidence.target: a child shall be born to the house of David, named Josias, and he shall immolate upon thee priests of the excelses

23:17.note: At Bethel Josias asks after the tomb of the man who, three centuries earlier, had named Josias himself against that altar. The history itself closes the prophecy's loop.

evidence.source: I have anointed thee king over the people of the Lord of Israel
evidence.target: Jehu the son of Namsi thou shalt anoint king over Israel

9:6.note: The young prophet at Ramoth Galaad does what Elias was charged to do on Horeb: Jehu is anointed king over Israel, a generation after the charge was given.

evidence.source: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the guarder thereof.
evidence.target: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the guider thereof.

13:14.note: Joas weeps over the dying Eliseus in Eliseus's own words over the ascending Elias — the cry is quoted, with only the last noun's spelling differing as printed (guarder/guider).

evidence.source: with the mantle of Elias, that fell down to him, he smote the waters, and they were not divided.
evidence.target: when Elias came to him, he cast his mantle upon him.

2:14.note: The mantle that fell at the ascension is the mantle cast on Eliseus at the plough: the call and the succession are one garment, and Eliseus proves it at the same river.

evidence.source: washed in Jordan seven times according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored
evidence.target: none of them was made clean but Naaman the Syrian

evidence.source: thou art the only God of all the kings of the earth: thou madest heaven and earth
evidence.target: thou art the only God of all the kingdoms of the earth, thou hast made heaven and earth

evidence.source: transport you into a land, that is like to your land, into a fruitful land, and plentiful of wine
evidence.target: take you away to a land, that is as your own, a land of corn and of wine

18:32.note: Rabsaces' surrender speech promising a land like their own, of corn and wine, is preserved in both Kings and Isaias.

evidence.source: Where is the king of Emath, and the king of Arphad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Ana and Ava?
evidence.target: Where is the king of Emath, and the king of Arphad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Ana, & Ava?

19:13.note: Sennacherib's taunting letter asks after the fallen kings of Emath and Arphad in identical words in Kings and Isaias.

evidence.source: save us from his hand, that all the Kingdoms of the earth may know, that thou art the Lord the only God
evidence.target: save us out of his hand: and let all the kingdoms of the earth know, that thou only art the Lord

19:19.note: Ezechias prays that all kingdoms may know the Lord alone is God, in the same words in Kings and Isaias.

evidence.source: out of Jerusalem there shall remnants go forth, and that which is to be saved from the mount of Sion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this
evidence.target: out of Jerusalem there shall a remnant go forth, and salvation from mount Sion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this

19:31.note: Isaiah's oracle of the remnant going forth from Jerusalem and Mount Sion stands in both histories.

evidence.source: And I will protect this city, and will save it for myself, and for David my servant
evidence.target: And I will protect this city, that I may save it for mine own sake, and for David's sake my servant

19:34.note: God's promise to protect Jerusalem for his own sake and David's is worded alike in Kings and Isaias.

evidence.source: I will add to thy days fifteen years: yea & out of the hand of the king of Assyrians I will deliver thee
evidence.target: Lo I will add upon thy days fifteen years

20:6.note: The fifteen added years promised to Ezechias, with deliverance from the Assyrian king, are given in both accounts.

evidence.source: Thus saith our Lord the God of Israel: Tell the man, that sent you to me
evidence.target: Thus saith our Lord the God of Israel: Tell the man, that sent you to me

22:15.note: Olda's oracle to Josias' messengers opens with the same charge in Kings and in Chronicles.

evidence.source: there was not such a Phase made from the days of the Judges, which judged Israel
evidence.target: There was not a Phase like to this in Israel, from the days of Samuel the Prophet

23:22.note: Josias' Passover is praised in both accounts as unmatched since the days of the Judges and of Samuel.

evidence.source: for the provocations, wherewith Manasses had provoked him
evidence.target: because of Manasses the son of Ezechias the king of Juda, for all things that he did in Jerusalem

23:26.note: Jeremias' scattering 'because of Manasses' explains the wrath Kings says still burned against Juda despite Josias.

evidence.source: transported the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and the fugitives, that were fled to the king of Babylon
evidence.target: of the fugitives, that were fled to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, Nabuzardan the Prince of the warfare transported

25:11.note: Nabuzardan's deportation of those remaining in the city and the fugitives is told in both Kings and Jeremias 52.

evidence.source: two pillars, one sea, and the feet which Salomon had made in the temple of our Lord: there was no weight of the brass of all the vessels
evidence.target: two pillars, & one sea, & twelve oxen of brass, that were under the feet, which king Salomon had made in the house of our Lord: there was no weight of the brass of all these vessels

25:16.note: Jeremias 52 repeats Kings' inventory of the temple bronze carried off: two pillars, one sea, and no weight to the brass.

evidence.source: he did eat bread always in his sight, all the days of his life
evidence.target: he did eat bread before him always all the days of his life

25:29.note: Joachin's release ends alike in both accounts: he ate bread before the king always, all the days of his life.

evidence.source: For we are pilgrims before thee, and strangers, as all our fathers
evidence.target: you are my strangers & sojourners

29:15.note: David's prayer over the temple treasury takes its self-understanding from the land law: because the land is God's, even Israel's king is his stranger and sojourner, and nothing dedicated is truly his own.

evidence.source: Our days are as a shadow upon the earth, and there is no abiding
evidence.target: flyeth as a shadow, and never abideth in the same state

29:15.note: David's prayer that our days are as a shadow with no abiding shares Job's image of man flying as a shadow.

evidence.source: Deal manfully, and take courage, and do it: fear not, and be not dismayed: for our Lord my God will be with thee, and will not leave thee, nor forsake thee
evidence.target: himself will be with thee: he will not leave, nor forsake thee: fear not, neither dread thou.

28:20.note: David hands the charge down a second time: as Moses charged Josue, so David charges Salomon, with the same promise in the same words — the charge of 31:6–7 and the promise of 31:8 in one breath.

evidence.source: Deal manfully, and take courage, and do it: fear not, and be not dismayed: for our Lord my God will be with thee, and will not leave thee, nor forsake thee
evidence.target: take courage, and be strong. Fear not, and dread not: because the Lord thy God is with thee

28:20.note: David charges Solomon with God's charge to Josue: take courage, fear not, the Lord will be with thee and not forsake thee.

evidence.source: Achar, who troubled Israel, and sinned in the theft of the anathema.
evidence.target: Because thou hast disturbed us, our Lord disturb thee in this day. And all Israel stoned him

2:7.note: Chronicles' genealogy remembers Achar (Josue's Achan) by his deed: he troubled Israel in the anathema's theft. Josue's sentence answers word for word — thou hast disturbed us — and ends in the stoning the genealogy presupposes.

evidence.source: Saul therefore caught his sword, and fell upon it.
evidence.target: Saul therefore caught his sword, and fell upon it.

10:4.note: Chronicles retells Saul's death in Samuel's words, the closing clause verbatim: refused by his armourbearer, Saul caught his sword and fell upon it. The same event told twice; Chronicles adds its own verdict at 10:13-14, which is its commentary, not a second entry.

evidence.source: But Satan rose against Israel: and moved David to number Israel.
evidence.target: stirred up David among them saying: Go, number Israel and Juda.

21:1.note: Chronicles retells the census in Samuel's shape — David moved to number Israel — but the two books name the mover differently, and the difference is stated, not harmonized: Samuel opens with the fury of the Lord stirring David up; Chronicles says Satan rose against Israel and moved him. The same event, told twice, with its tension on the page.

evidence.source: they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of our Lord, which he spake in the hand of Samuel.
evidence.target: they anointed David to be king over Israel.

11:3.note: David made king over all Israel at Hebron, in both histories; Chronicles adds that it was according to the word spoken by Samuel.

evidence.source: Our Lord therefore was angry against Oza, & struck him, for that he had touched the Ark: and he died there before our Lord.
evidence.target: our Lord was wrath with indignation against Oza, and struck him for the rashness: who died there before the ark of God.

13:10.note: Oza struck at the ark's first bringing up, in Samuel and in Chronicles.

evidence.source: I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to me for a son
evidence.target: I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to me for a son

17:13.note: Nathan's oracle in both histories, word for word at its centre: the son of David held in a father-son covenant.

evidence.source: David struck the Philisthiims, and humbled them
evidence.target: David struck the Philisthiims, and humbled them

18:1.note: The wars of David open in both histories with the same sentence; what David took differs in the verses' second halves (Geth in Chronicles, the bridle of tribute in Samuel), and is left as printed.

evidence.source: at such time when kings are wont to go forth to battle, Joab gathered together the army
evidence.target: at such time when kings are wont to proceed to battles, David sent Joab

20:1.note: The Rabba campaign opens with the same season formula; Chronicles passes over the Bathsabee matter that fills Samuel's chapter. The seed carries the pair only at chapter level (2 Kings 11).

evidence.source: Thou hast shed much blood, and fought very many battles, thou canst not build a house to my name
evidence.target: Shalt thou build me a house to dwell in?

22:8.note: Chronicles gives the reason Samuel's oracle leaves unstated: the man of blood may not build. Samuel records the refusal; Chronicles records its ground.

evidence.source: Joab the son of Sarvia began to number, and finished not: because upon this there fell wrath upon Israel
evidence.target: Our Lord therefore sent the pestilence in Israel: and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.

27:24.note: Within Chronicles itself: the registrar's note that the census number was never registered points back to the plague chapter it came from.

evidence.source: know the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart
evidence.target: keep his ceremonies, and his precepts & judgments, and testimonies as is written in the law of Moyses

28:9.note: David's charge to Salomon stands in two forms: Chronicles' assembly charge (know God, serve him, seek and find) and Kings' deathbed charge (walk in his ways, keep the law of Moyses). Graded parallel — same charge, different words preserved.

evidence.source: the sons of Phares, Hesron and Hamul.
evidence.target: Phares begat Esron

2:5.note: Juda's line in the genealogies meets Ruth's closing genealogy at Phares and Hesron (Esron), the line that runs to David.

evidence.source: The children of Amram: Aaron, Moyses, and Maria.
evidence.target: who bare him Aaron & Moyses.

6:3.note: The priestly genealogy's head in Chronicles against its source in Exodus: Amram's children are Aaron, Moyses and Maria.

evidence.source: According to all these words, & according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David
evidence.target: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so spake Nathan to David

7:17.note: Nathan delivers the oracle to David according to all these words and this vision, in identical terms in both tellings.

evidence.source: there is none like to thee, neither is there a God besides thee
evidence.target: one nation in the earth, to the which God went, to deliver it and make it his people

7:22.note: David's prayer after the oracle — no God besides thee, one nation God went to deliver — is prayed in both tellings.

evidence.source: David said to Nathan: I have sinned to our Lord
evidence.target: when Nathan the Prophet came to him, after that he had sinned with Bethsabee

12:13.note: David's 'I have sinned to our Lord' to Nathan is the confession Psalm 50's heading ties to Nathan's coming after Bethsabee.

evidence.source: Our Lord is my rock, and my strength, and my Saviour
evidence.target: Our Lord is my firmament, and my refuge, and my deliverer

22:2.note: David's song in Samuel and Psalm 17 are the same hymn, opening with the Lord as rock, refuge and deliverer.

evidence.source: In my tribulation I will invocate our Lord, & I will cry to my God: and he will hear my voice out of his holy temple
evidence.target: In my tribulation I have invocated our Lord, and have cried to my God: And he hath heard my voice from his holy temple

22:7.note: The same verse of David's song stands in both places: in tribulation he cried, and was heard from the holy temple.

evidence.source: With the elect thou shalt be elect: and with the perverse thou shalt be perverted
evidence.target: And with the elect thou shalt be elect: and with the perverse thou shalt be perverted

22:27.note: David's song and Psalm 17 carry the identical couplet on God's dealing with the elect and the perverse.

evidence.source: the word of our Lord is examined by fire: he is the shield of all that trust in him
evidence.target: the words of our Lord are examined by fire: he is protector of all that hope in him

22:31.note: Both versions of the song confess God's immaculate way and his words examined by fire.

evidence.source: Our Lord liveth, and my God is blessed: and the strong God of my salvation shall be exalted
evidence.target: Our Lord liveth, and blessed be my God, and the God of my salvation be exalted

22:47.note: The song's climax 'Our Lord liveth' and the exaltation of the God of his salvation stand in both Samuel and the Psalm.

evidence.source: build an altar to our Lord in the floor of Areuna the Jebuseite
evidence.target: in the place, which David had prepared in the floor of Ornan the Jebusite

24:18.note: The threshingfloor where Gad bids David build his altar is the place David prepared, where Solomon began the house on Mount Moria.

evidence.source: What is man that thou magnifiest him? Or why settest thou thy heart toward him?
evidence.target: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? Or the son of man, that thou visitest him?

7:17.note: Job asks the psalm's wonder-question in affliction's key: what is man, that God should regard him. Entered as a verbal echo between the two books, without asserting which text was written first.

evidence.source: By a dream in a vision by night, when heavy sleep falleth upon men
evidence.target: in vision will I appear to him, or in sleep I will speak to him.

33:15.note: Elihu's doctrine of God's night-speaking — by a dream in a vision, when heavy sleep falls — rests on the Lord's own word to Aaron and Mary: in vision he appears, in sleep he speaks.

evidence.source: Behold the fear of our Lord, that is wisdom: and to depart from evil, understanding.
evidence.target: The fear of our Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

28:28.note: The wisdom hymn ends where Proverbs begins: the fear of the Lord is wisdom itself. Job's form — that is wisdom — and Solomon's — the beginning of wisdom — state the one sentence from its two ends.

evidence.source: the fear of our Lord, that is wisdom: and to depart from evil, understanding
evidence.target: the fear of our Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Understanding is good to all that do it

28:28.note: Job's conclusion that the fear of the Lord is wisdom and departing from evil understanding is the psalm's beginning-of-wisdom confession.

evidence.source: Did not he make me in the womb that made him also
evidence.target: The rich and poor have met one another: our Lord is the maker of both.

31:15.note: Job pleads his servants' cause from the proverb's ground before Solomon states it: one Maker made master and servant in the womb, as rich and poor have one Maker of both.

evidence.source: the name of our Lord be blessed
evidence.target: The name of our Lord be blessed

evidence.source: man is not justified compared with God
evidence.target: no man living shall be justified in thy sight

evidence.source: Why didst thou bring me forth out of the matrice?
evidence.target: Why came I out of the womb, that I should see labour and sorrow

evidence.source: Man born of woman, living a short time, is replenished with many miseries
evidence.target: from the day of their coming forth of their mother's womb, until the day of their burying

evidence.source: my bone hath cleaved to my skin
evidence.target: my bone hath cleaved to my flesh

evidence.source: the shining stars Pleiades, or canst thou dissipate the circuit of Arcturus?
evidence.target: Him that maketh Arcturus, and Orion

evidence.source: I know that thou canst do all things
evidence.target: thou hast mercy on all, because thou canst do all things

evidence.source: Blessed is the man that is corrected of God: refuse not therefore the chastising of our Lord
evidence.target: cast not away the discipline of our Lord: neither do thou faint when thou art chastised of him

5:17.note: Eliphaz's beatitude on the man corrected by God is the wisdom Proverbs presses on the son not to refuse the Lord's chastising.

evidence.source: what is the place of understanding?
evidence.target: Who hath found the place thereof?

28:20.note: Baruch takes up Job's unanswered question after wisdom's place, asking who has found the place of understanding and entered her treasures.

evidence.source: Let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my simplicity
evidence.target: thou art weighed in the balance, and art found having less

31:6.note: Job's appeal to be weighed in a just balance is answered in kind at Belshazzar's feast, where the king is weighed in the balance and found wanting.

evidence.source: our Lord blessed the last days of Job
evidence.target: we account them blessed that have suffered. The sufferance of Job you have heard

42:12.note: James's blessed sufferers and the heard sufferance of Job point back to this verse, where the Lord blessed Job's last days more than his beginning.

evidence.source: I know that my Redeemer liveth, & in the last day I shall rise out of the earth
evidence.target: I am the resurrection and the life; he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live

19:25.note: Job's confession of a living Redeemer and his own rising in the last day is the doctrine Christ speaks in his own person at Bethany.

evidence.source: in my flesh I shall see God
evidence.target: I in justice shall appear to thy sight: I shall be filled when thy glory shall appear

19:26.note: Job's hope to see God in his flesh answers the psalmist's hope to appear to God's sight and be filled when his glory appears.

evidence.source: Who doeth great and unsearchable and marvelous things without number
evidence.target: his ways unsearchable

5:9.note: Paul's doxology on God's unsearchable ways takes up Eliphaz's confession of the God who does great and unsearchable things without number.

evidence.source: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding
evidence.target: wisdom and strength are his

12:13.note: Daniel's blessing of God because wisdom and strength are his repeats Job's confession that with God is wisdom and strength.

evidence.source: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?
evidence.target: when he hanged the foundations of the earth

38:4.note: God's question to Job about the foundations of the earth is the scene Wisdom describes from her own place beside him at the founding.

evidence.source: If we confess our sins, he is faithful & just, for to forgive us our sins
evidence.target: he that shall confess, and shall forsake them, shall obtain mercy.

1:9.note: The proverb's promise — he that confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy — is the ground of John's: if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive.

evidence.source: He that shall have the substance of the world, and shall see his brother have need, and shall shut his bowels from him
evidence.target: He that stoppeth his ear at the cry of the poor, himself also shall cry and shall not be heard.

3:17.note: The proverb's stopped ear against the poor man's cry becomes John's shut bowels against the brother in need; both ask how a man so closed can stand before God.

evidence.source: he that came by water & blood Jesus Christ: not in water only, but in water and blood
evidence.target: there came forth blood and water

5:6.note: John's epistle bears witness to what his Gospel saw at the cross: the blood and water that came forth from the opened side — 'not in water only, but in water and blood.'

evidence.source: which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the word of life
evidence.target: The Word Was Made Flesh, and dwelt in us (and we saw the glory of him

1:1.note: The epistle opens on the Gospel's prologue: the Word of life seen with eyes and handled with hands is the Word made flesh, whose glory 'we saw'.

evidence.source: that you may know that you have eternal life which believe in the name of the Son of God.
evidence.target: that believing, you may have life in his name.

5:13.note: John's letter states its purpose in the Gospel's own terms: believing in the Son's name, his readers have life in his name.

evidence.source: you have no need that any man teach you: but as his unction teacheth you of all things,
evidence.target: a man shall no more teach his neighbour, and a man his brother, saying: Know our Lord: for all shall know me

2:27.note: The unction teaching the faithful so none need teach them in 1 John fulfils Jeremias's new-covenant word that no man shall teach his neighbour to know the Lord.

evidence.source: Whosoever hateth his brother, is a murderer.
evidence.target: Cain rose up against his brother Abel, and slew him.

3:15.note: Hatred of a brother counted as murder in 1 John is measured against Cain, the first brother-hater, who slew Abel.

evidence.source: Whatsoever you do, work it from the heart as to our Lord, and not to men
evidence.target: Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, work it instantly

3:23.note: Paul's household rule is the Preacher's urgency with its reason changed: whatsoever thy hand is able to do, work it — instantly, says Ecclesiastes, for there is no work in hell; from the heart as to the Lord, says the apostle.

evidence.source: where Christ is sitting on the right hand of God.
evidence.target: Sit on my right hand

3:1.note: Seeking the things above is located by the psalm's oracle: Christ seated at the right hand where the Lord set his Lord. Hebrews 1:13's quotation of the same verse is seed-carried.

evidence.source: teaching and admonishing your own selves, with psalms, hymns, and spiritual canticles, in grace singing in your hearts to God.
evidence.target: speaking to yourselves in Psalms & hymns, and spiritual canticles, chanting and singing in your hearts to our Lord:

3:16.note: Near-identical charge in both letters: psalms, hymns and spiritual canticles, singing in the heart — at Ephesus the fruit of the Spirit's fullness, at Colosse of Christ's word dwelling richly.

evidence.source: which are a shadow of things to come, but the body Christ's.
evidence.target: the law having a shadow of good things to come, not the very image of the things:

2:17.note: Both letters call the old observances a shadow of coming goods, against the body and reality that is Christ's.

evidence.source: hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love,
evidence.target: this is your hour, and the power of darkness.

1:13.note: Deliverance from the power of darkness in Colossians answers the hour of the power of darkness at the Lord's arrest.

evidence.source: The Mandragoræs have given a smell.
evidence.target: found mandragoras: which he brought to his mother Lia

7:13.note: The bride's mandrakes at the gates are Rachel's mandrakes of the wheat harvest, the love-fruit Ruben found in the field and Lia's son brought home. The corpus spells the word Mandragoræs in the Canticle and mandragoras in Genesis; the plant and its errand are the same.

evidence.source: the well of living waters
evidence.target: a fountain of water springing up unto life everlasting

evidence.source: if a man shall give all the substance of his house for love
evidence.target: he shall restore sevenfold, and shall give up all the substance of his house

evidence.source: come up from the lavatory, all with twins, and there is no barren among them
evidence.target: come up from the lavatory, all with twins, and there is no barren among them

4:2.note: The bride's praise is sung twice in the Canticle, the teeth as shorn flocks from the lavatory, all with twins and none barren.

evidence.source: My beloved to me, and I to him, who feedeth among the lilies
evidence.target: my beloved to me, who feedeth among the lilies

2:16.note: The mutual-possession refrain, my beloved to me and I to him who feeds among the lilies, returns in the Canticle's later song.

evidence.source: he delivered the same to keepers
evidence.target: I will sing to my beloved the canticle of my cousin concerning his vineyard

8:11.note: Both songs sing a beloved's vineyard delivered to keepers, the Canticle's peace-maker's vineyard and Isaias's canticle of his beloved's vineyard.

evidence.source: in the name of Jesus every knee bow of the celestials, terrestrials, and infernals:
evidence.target: every knee shall be bowed to me, and every tongue shall swear

2:10.note: Every knee bowing, transferred to the name of Jesus. The seed keys Romans 14:11 to this verse and this verse of Philippians to 45:14; the hymn's own anchor is 45:23.

evidence.source: whose names are in the book of life.
evidence.target: I will not put his name out of the book of life,

4:3.note: Paul's fellow-labourers are known by the same register John is promised from: names in the book of life, and not blotted out of it. Exodus 32:33's striking-out stands behind both and is keyed at Apocalypse's verse.

evidence.source: whose names are in the book of life
evidence.target: every one that shall be found written in the book

evidence.source: in the midst of a crooked and perverse Generation
evidence.target: a froward and perverse generation

evidence.source: every tongue confess that our Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.
evidence.target: every knee shall be bowed to me, and every tongue shall swear.

2:11.note: The universal confession of Jesus as Lord in Philippians fulfils God's oath in Isaias that every tongue shall swear to him.

evidence.source: our conversation is in Heaven: whence also we expect the Saviour
evidence.target: they desire a better, that is to say, a heavenly. Therefore God is not confounded to be called their God.

3:20.note: Citizenship in heaven in Philippians matches the patriarchs' desire for the better, heavenly country in Hebrews.

evidence.source: he sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself as though he were God
evidence.target: shall be elevated, & magnified against every god: and against the God of gods he shall speak magnifical things

2:4.note: The man of sin extolled above all called God, shewing himself as God, is Daniel's king magnified against every god, speaking magnifical things against the God of gods. The temple-sitting detail is Paul's; the self-magnifying against God is Daniel's, and only that is claimed.

evidence.source: whom our Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth; and shall destroy with the manifestation of his advent
evidence.target: to have perished by the blast of God, and with the spirit of his wrath to have been consumed.

2:8.note: Eliphaz' word — perishing by God's blast, consumed by the spirit of his wrath — becomes the manner of the wicked one's destruction: slain by the spirit of the Lord Jesus' mouth. Isaias 11:4's rod-of-his-mouth strand is seed-carried for this verse.

evidence.source: in flame of fire, giving revenge to them that know not God
evidence.target: our Lord will come in fire, & his chariots as a whirlwind, to render his fury in indignation, & his rebuking in flame of fire:

1:8.note: The Lord coming in fire with rebuking in flame of fire is Isaias' last-chapter theophany; Paul's advent in flame of fire renders revenge in the same element.

evidence.source: from the face of our Lord and from the glory of his power:
evidence.target: from the face of the fear of our Lord, and from the glory of his majesty

1:9.note: Destruction away from the Lord's face and the glory of his power echoes Isaias's flight from the face and glory of the Lord.

evidence.source: If the grape gatherers had entered in to thee, would they not have left thee at the least a cluster?
evidence.target: If the grape gatherers had come upon thee, they had not left a cluster

1:5.note: Abdias' Edom oracle and Jeremias' Edom oracle (ch. 49) share whole sentences; the seed carries Abdias 1:1 -> Jeremias 49 at chapter level only. Verse anchors are filled in this and the next two entries.

evidence.source: How have they searched Esau, have they sought out his hidden things?
evidence.target: I have discovered Esau, I have revealed his secrets, and he cannot be concealed

1:6.note: The searching of Esau, common to both Edom oracles.

evidence.source: destroy the wise out of Idumea, and prudence from the mount of Esau
evidence.target: Why is wisdom no more in Theman? Counsel is perished from the children

1:8.note: The wisdom of Edom destroyed — Jeremias asks why wisdom is no more in Theman, Abdias answers with its destruction.

evidence.source: If thou shalt be exalted as an eagle, and if thou shalt set thy nest among the stars: thence will I pluck thee down
evidence.target: When thou shalt exalt thy nest as an eagle, thence will I bring thee down

evidence.source: as you have drunk upon my holy mount, shall all Gentiles drink continually
evidence.target: drink thou also, and be fast a sleep: the cup of the right hand of our Lord shall compass thee

evidence.source: And in mount Sion shall be salvation
evidence.target: in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem shall be salvation

evidence.source: when strangers took his army, and foreigners entered his gates, and upon Jerusalem cast lot
evidence.target: Be mindful, o Lord, of the children of Edom, in the day of Jerusalem

1:11.note: The psalm's plea to remember the children of Edom in Jerusalem's day matches Abdias's charge: Edom stood by while strangers entered the gates and cast lots upon Jerusalem.

evidence.source: the house of Esau stubble: and they shall be kindled in them, and shall devour them
evidence.target: all that do impiety shall be stubble: & the day coming shall inflame them

1:18.note: Malachias's furnace day, when all who do impiety shall be stubble inflamed by the coming day, takes up Abdias's house of Esau become stubble to Jacob's fire.

evidence.source: the day of our Lord shall so come, as a thief in the night
evidence.target: if the good-man of the house did know what hour the thief would come, he would surely watch

5:2.note: Paul's 'day of the Lord as a thief in the night' is the Lord's own householder image from the discourse: the thief who comes at an unknown hour, against whom the good-man watches.

evidence.source: having suffered before and been abused with contumelies (as you know) at Philippi
evidence.target: the magistrates tearing their coats, commanded them to be beaten with rods

2:2.note: Paul reminds the Thessalonians — 'as you know' — of the Philippi abuse Luke narrates: the magistrates tearing the coats and the beating with rods before the gaol.

evidence.source: having on, the breast-plate of faith and charity, and a helmet, the hope of salvation.
evidence.target: clothed with the breast-plate of justice,

5:8.note: The same armour worn twice by Paul, honestly noted: at Ephesus the breastplate is justice, to the Thessalonians faith and charity, and the helmet hope of salvation against Ephesians' helmet of salvation — the pieces are shared, their assignment differs.

evidence.source: so always we shall be with our Lord.
evidence.target: I come again and will take you to myself, that where I am, you also may be.

4:17.note: Being always with the Lord after the taking-up in Thessalonians is the promise of John 14 that he will take his own to himself.

evidence.source: let us not sleep as also others: but let us watch & be sober.
evidence.target: it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep.

5:6.note: Both letters urge watchfulness with the same image of rising from sleep because salvation is near.

evidence.source: Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry
evidence.target: Barnabas would have taken with them John also that was surnamed Mark

4:11.note: The Mark over whom Paul and Barnabas parted in Acts — John surnamed Mark — is the Mark the aged Paul asks for by name: 'profitable to me for the ministry.' The parting and the recall belong to one story.

evidence.source: Our Lord knoweth, who be his
evidence.target: In the morning our Lord will make it known who pertain to him, and the holy he will join to himself

2:19.note: In Core's rebellion Moses says the Lord will make known who are his; Paul sets that sentence as the seal on God's foundation against Hymeneus' gangrene.

evidence.source: if we be dead with him, we shall live also together.
evidence.target: if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall live also together with Christ.

2:11.note: The faithful saying in Timothy repeats in compressed form Romans' confession that those dead with Christ shall live with him.

evidence.source: who hath destroyed death, and illuminated life and incorruption by the Gospel:
evidence.target: He shall cast death down headlong for ever:

1:10.note: Christ destroying death at his appearing fulfils Isaias's prophecy that God shall cast death down for ever.

evidence.source: which he promised that lieth not, God, before the secular times:
evidence.target: God is not as man, that he may lie, nor as the son of man, that he may be changed.

1:2.note: The God who cannot lie, of Balaam's oracle, is the God who promised eternal life before the secular times; Titus 1:12's Cretan poet is not Scripture and is not keyed.

evidence.source: that he might redeem us from all iniquity
evidence.target: he shall redeem Israel, from all his iniquities

evidence.source: he hath saved us by the laver of regeneration
evidence.target: I will pour out upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your contaminations

evidence.source: Let no man contemn thee.
evidence.target: Let no man contemn thy youth:

2:15.note: The closing charge to Titus repeats the charge to Timothy that no man be allowed to despise the young minister.

evidence.source: not as a servant, but for a servant, a most dear brother, especially to me,
evidence.target: with Onesimus, the most dear and faithful brother who is of you.

1:16.note: The Onesimus Philemon must receive no longer as a servant but as a most dear brother is the same Onesimus Colossians calls the most dear and faithful brother.

evidence.source: many seducers are gone out into the world, which do not confess Jesus Christ to have come into flesh: this is a seducer and an Antichrist.
evidence.target: Every spirit that confesseth Jesus Christ to have come in flesh, is of God:

1:7.note: The second letter's test of the seducers restates the first letter's test of spirits by confession of Jesus Christ come in the flesh.

evidence.source: not as writing a new commandment to thee, but that which we have had from the beginning, that we love one another.
evidence.target: I write not a new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning.

1:5.note: Both Johannine letters insist the commandment to love is not new but the old commandment had from the beginning.

evidence.source: He that doeth well, is of God: he that doeth ill, hath not seen God.
evidence.target: every one that sinneth, hath not seen him, nor known him.

1:11.note: The third letter's rule that the evildoer has not seen God repeats the first letter's word that everyone who sins has not seen him.
